summary: Evidence delivery: presigned S3 object-lock export + tenant field-mapping for auditor e-discovery
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a cryptographically verifiable evidence bundle for a legal e-discovery request that covers a 21-day window across two production regions. Deliverables requested: presigned S3 export with Object Lock (governance mode), SHA-256 manifest and Merkle-tree-style checksum file, per-object KMS key metadata (customer-managed key id), and a mapping CSV that translates Redwood audit field names to the customer’s Tableau/EDS column names.

Impact:
Acme Health is under a timeboxed subpoena discovery window; failure to provide the requested artifacts by the legal deadline risks escalation to legal and potential regulatory penalties. They have flagged this as high priority and require chain-of-custody proof.

Environment:
Production audit pipeline for tenant: acme-health-prod. Primary regions involved: us-west and eu-central. Expected event types: session.audit, api.request, auth.activity.

Requested export specification (customer-provided):
- Time window: 2026-02-08T00:00:00Z to 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z (inclusive)
- Delivery mechanism: presigned S3 objects in a Redwood-managed bucket; objects must have Object Lock set to Governance mode with retention-until 2027-03-01.
- Encryption: SSE-KMS using customer-managed key (provide KMS key ARN). Include kms_key_id metadata in manifest.
- Integrity proof: per-object SHA256 and a top-level Merkle root file; manifest must include object name, size, SHA256, timestamp, and tenant-id.
- Field handling: PII fields identified by the customer must be pseudonymized in a separate pseudonymization mapping file; original raw events should be included in the export but delivered in a separate folder with restricted ACL.
- Schema mapping: Provide CSV that maps Redwood audit fields (e.g., event_type, ts, actor_id, resource, request_id) to Acme Health’s Data Warehouse column names and the Tableau friendly headers.
- Sample dataset: Customer requests a 24-hour representative sample before full export to validate mapping and KMS access.

Steps to reproduce / Access required:
1) Customer will share IAM role ARN and KMS key ARN with Support.
2) Support triggers a dry-run sample export for 2026-02-15 00:00–23:59 UTC to acme-health-sample/ folder.
3) Customer validates fields and signed manifest.
4) Full export performed and presigned links shared via encrypted ticket channel.

Security & compliance constraints:
- All artifacts must be accessible only via the presigned URLs; do not send raw credentials.
- Include certificate-chain info for signing process and time-stamped signature (RFC3161) if available.
- Provide a short attestation note that the export was produced from immutable audit snapshots and steps taken to ensure non-repudiation.

Preferred timeline:
- Sample export: within 48 hours of receiving IAM/KMS details.
- Full export: within 4 business days after sample sign-off.

Contact & escalation:
Primary contact: Grace Liu (Acme Health, grace.liu@acmehealth.example)
Legal contact: Mark Denton (Acme Legal)
Redwood account owner: Juan Ramirez

Additional notes: Customer specifically requested not to include full request bodies for any events flagged as 'medical_payload' in the raw export; instead, include a redaction flag and pointer to a secure, access-controlled dataset that can be provided under additional legal guardrails.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Sofia Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Please share the IAM role ARN and KMS key ARN. We'll commence a 24-hour sample within 48 hours after we have access. Escalating to compliance for attestation details.

2026-03-11 14:28 - Compliance Team (internal): Need to confirm whether RFC3161 timestamping is available for export signing; also confirm if we can provide Merkle-root generation. Looping SRE and Storage.

2026-03-12 11:03 - SRE (internal): Can produce sample export and generate SHA256 per object. Object Lock can be applied at object-level for presigned objects only if bucket has Object Lock and Object Lock configuration applied at upload. Need confirmation if customer prefers customer-managed bucket or Redwood-managed bucket with customer KMS.
investigation_notes: Initial feasibility check completed 2026-03-11. Storage team confirmed we can generate per-object SHA256 and a Merkle root. Object Lock requires bucket-level configuration; for Redwood-managed bucket we need to set Governance retention during upload. Customer must provide KMS key with grants to Redwoods service principal. Engineering raised a cryptographic signing question: timestamping via RFC3161 is not currently automated in the export path; can generate detached signature using a Redwood archival-signing service if Compliance signs off.
workaround: Until export is complete, Support provided a filtered search query and a secure screening export for legal review (redacted bodies) through secure link. Customer accepted sample approach to validate mapping.
next_steps: 1) Customer to provide IAM role ARN and KMS key ARN. 2) Support to schedule sample export and share presigned URLs. 3) Compliance to confirm signing/attestation language. 4) After sample approval, schedule full export and apply Object Lock on upload. 5) Deliver manifest and mapping CSV, then close ticket.
